items.note: Trailōkyavarman's inscription slab is set above a house door in front of the Jaina temple at Vidishā; discovered in 1969.
Records construction of a temple of Murāri, probably by king Trailōkyavarman, with donations; date Chaitra vadi 12, Vikrama 1216.
Stanzas 4-6 describe a lofty temple of Murārī in boar-incarnation; place evidently Vidishā itself, from mention of river Vētravatī.
Trailōkyavarman imposed a tax of a vimśōpaka on every load on a bull, evidently in favour of the temple.
Vidishā inscription: Trailōkyavarman laid a tax of one viṇśōpaka on every load on a bull; genealogy not given.
Vētravatī of v. 7 is the well known river Betwā flowing by Vidishā.
Trailōkyavarman belonged to the Mahākumāra branch of Paramāras, apparently regent during nephew Harischandra's minority; Harischandra had issued a grant from Vidishā in V.S. 1214.

items.note: Gyāraspur grant by Mahākumāra Trailōkyavarmadēva, evidently of the subordinate Paramāra branch around Bhopāl; pedigree not specified.
Following Chakravarti, Trailōkyavarman acted as regent during Harischandra's minority.
Chandēlas had annexed region near Gyāraspur from the Paramāras, per Madanavarman's Augasī grant issued from Bhilsā (Vidishā).

items.note: Mahākumāra Harischandra donated village Dādarapadra in the Mahādvādaśaka-maṇḍala, divided into 16 shares among 19 Brāhmaṇas.
Harischandra's grant names Naravarmadēva, Yasōvarmadēva, Trailōkyavarmadēva and Harischandra; Harischandra obtained his principality through Trailōkyavarman's favour.
Two Harischandra grants credit different sovereigns (Trailōkyavarman, Jayavarman); victory may allude to the Chandēlas, their northern neighbours.
